problem: Textual CoT in VLN lacks spatial grounding and overfits sparse annotated reasoning, while multimodal CoT that generates imagined observations causes severe token inflation (3k-5k tokens per 5-7 actions), making real-time navigation impractical.
motivation: Long-horizon, multi-stage navigation (LH-VLN) needs joint semantic planning and spatial understanding, but explicit CoT is too slow and error-prone over long trajectories. The authors want CoT benefits without CoT decoding cost at inference, following Aux-Think's train-with-CoT, infer-without-CoT idea.
key_idea: Jointly train one VLM under gated non-CoT, textual, VAR-latent visual and multimodal CoT modes, aligning all CoT-mode action predictions to the non-CoT mode, then infer with direct non-CoT action prediction only.
insight: The mode ablation shows every CoT mode helps the non-CoT policy (ISR 2.01 non-CoT alone to 11.01 with all modes), and removing cross-mode alignment collapses performance (SR 2.44 to 0, ISR 11.01 to 2.39). Implicit inference beats explicit CoT decoding in the multimodal case (SR 2.44 vs 0.98), suggesting explicit CoT accumulates errors and overfits on the small LH-VLN data. Visual reasoning in a compact VAR latent space (scale 4 best) trains far faster than pixel-level V-CoT (WorldVLA).
method: CompV-CoT: Qwen2.5-VL predicts a few low-scale latent tokens of a frozen pretrained VAR (next-scale prediction; scale 4 selected) as imagined future observations, giving about 1/2185 compression instead of pixel tokens; no VAR decoding at inference.

Textual CoT: Qwen-VL-Max annotates all 18,554 LH-VLN training slices with a structured trace (semantic plan, visual description, action planning, visual imagination); the agent generates this before actions.
Multimodal CoT: paired textual and visual-latent reasoning steps M_t=[T_t,V_t] generated before actions.
Gated unified policy: two binary gating tokens (g_T, g_V) select non-CoT, T-CoT, V-CoT or MM-CoT modes in one shared model, with the modes uniformly sampled during training and a joint CE loss.

Cross-mode alignment: the non-CoT mode is optimized with CE to GT actions, then its stop-gradient action prediction serves as soft targets for the action outputs of the T/V/MM modes (L_Align + L_CoT), alternating the two objectives.
Inference: non-CoT mode only, predicting 5 actions per step by direct token decoding.
Training setup: LoRA on Qwen2.5-VL, history-frame augmentation (subsampling and trimming), 64 H20 GPUs.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL (LoRA fine-tuned) with frozen pretrained VAR as visual latent decoder/target
setting.training_data: LH-VLN training set (18,554 five-action trajectory slices) with Qwen-VL-Max generated textual CoT annotations and VAR latent tokens of future frames; history augmentation
setting.observation: egocentric RGB: left/front/right current views plus up to ~20 historical front-view images
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward, left, right, stop (5 actions predicted per step)

results: On LH-VLN, FantasyVLN reaches SR 2.44 / ISR 11.01 / CSR 9.64 / CGT 8.99, beating the strongest baseline Aux-Think (0.65 / 3.16 / 2.04 / 1.47) and MGDM on CGT (2.91). It runs at 1.03 APS versus 0.19 for explicit CoT-VLA, a roughly 5x speedup, with similar speed to other implicit methods.
limitations: Evaluated only on LH-VLN, where absolute success rates remain very low (SR 2.44%).
Baselines Aux-Think and CoT-VLA are re-implemented from their papers, and the explicit-CoT modes underperform implicit inference, so the explicit reasoning is not actually exploited at test time.
Depends on a VAR compressor with high reconstruction MSE (0.039) and on LLM-generated CoT annotations; heavy training compute (64 H20 GPUs).
